reconcile.note: Jamieson, Fausset, and Brown treat Romans 5:12's blame on Adam as his role as federal head, distinct from 1 Timothy 2:14's point that Eve's deception grounds women's subjection.

discrepancy.note: Ingersoll quotes 1 Timothy's Adam-not-deceived, Eve-deceived reasoning as the only basis given for blaming the fall on Eve rather than Adam.

quotes.text: Adam was first formed, and then Eve … Adam was not deceived … the woman being deceived, was in the transgression. … These childish reasons are the only ones given by the inspired writers.
quotes.attr: Robert G. Ingersoll (d. 1899), The Christian Religion, pt. III (1881), on 1 Timothy 2:13-14 and the blame for the fall.

sides.snippet: Therefore, as sin entered into the world through one man, and death through sin; and so death passed to all men, because all sinned.
sides.verseText: Therefore, as sin entered into the world through one man, and death through sin; and so death passed to all men, because all sinned.

sides.snippet: Adam wasn't deceived, but the woman, being deceived, has fallen into disobedience;
